Journalist Johnny Mitchell reports to Danny Jones on Mexico's teenage narco-militias, which he says are deadlier than ever. Mitchell has covered cartel country closely, and his dispatch focuses on the cartels' youngest recruits. The child soldiers are getting younger as the wars get worse.

Mitchell explains how cartels recruit teens with money, status, and fear. He describes the training and violence these young fighters both suffer and inflict. Jones asks what it means for Mexico and for the border towns Americans know. Sober and concerned listeners get a grim report from a reporter who goes where the story is.

Jake James, billed as the real Florida Man, joins Danny Jones for KONCRETE number 49. The title promises prescription drugs and heavy metal. The sample opens with a wild tooth story instead.

James recalls rollerblading at school and cracking a tooth. A dentist glued it on a weekend visit. Hours later, wrestling knocked the same tooth out again. From there the talk rolls into drugs, music, and Florida chaos. The episode has the loose, funny feel of friends swapping tales that sound too strange to invent. Nothing in the hour feels scripted or safe.
